catalog_quote: Quanto ao padrão acentual do Tembé e do Guajajára há ocorrência de acento na última sílaba da palavra, quando esta é formada por duas sílabas ou mais. [za"nE] 'nós' [ha"muj] 'avô dele' [pa"kO] 'banana' [ta"hÈw] 'formiga' [ka"/i] 'macaco' [miri"kur] 'lombriga' ... O acento também ocorre na penúltima sílaba, fequentemente nos temas nominais flexionados por sufixos de caso ou de temas nominais ou verbais flexionados pelo sufixo de negação -i. Os exemplos a seguir aplicam-se tanto ao Tembé quanto ao Guajajára. [hE|´"pÈjmE] 'em minha casa' [nO"hE0õmI*0] 'ele não sai' [i"dzarø*] 'dono dele' [naipi"hu0nI0*] 'ele não é preto'

new_statements.quote: O acento recai na sílaba final de palavras como substantivos e verbos, e nas posposições quando essas ocorrem com prefixos.
new_statements.translation: Stress falls on the final syllable of words such as nouns and verbs, and on postpositions when these occur with prefixes.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: extracted text of (474 pp.) gives, in Introdução section 3.B after the consonant table and the <kw>/<gw> remark, exactly: 'O acento recai na sílaba final de palavras como substantivos e verbos, e nas posposições quando essas ocorrem com prefixos.' PDF page 3 = printed page 3 (page-number footer '3' follows a few lines later). A dictionary-wide a full-text search for stress/accent acento/tônic/stress finds no other stress statement (only the lexical entry 'íngreme, acentuado: iàpy'àm'). Reading fixed: final syllable is right; with the catalog rule empty and no existing statements, 'refines' (fills the empty record) is the right relation. Identity: p. 2 says the Guajajara-Tenetehar speak 'uma…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog holds a record for this language with an EMPTY rule and no existing statements, so this is the first placement statement found: fixed final stress. The dictionary is explicitly pan-dialectal Guajajara-Tenetehar (introduction, p. 2: 'Fala-se uma única língua tupi-guarani, porém com cinco dialetos', Tembé being the most divergent), compiled from data begun in 1961 by David and Margaret Bendor-Samuel and continued by the Harrisons from 1970, mainly at Campo Alegre / Posto Zutíua (Araribóia area, Maranhão).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of nouns and verbs; a postposition is stressed (on its final syllable) only when it carries a prefix, which implies that bare postpositions are unstressed/clitic-like.
new_statements.exceptions: Postpositions: stressed only when prefixed (otherwise, by implication, unstressed). No other exceptions given; the statement is one sentence and gives no examples or stress marks in the entries (the orthography does not mark stress).
new_statements.identity_note: Harrison & Harrison 2013 describe Guajajara-Tenetehar as one language with five dialects (Corda/Mearim, Grajaú, Pindaré, Zutíua/Araribóia, and Tembé, the most divergent) and worked mainly at Campo Alegre / Posto Zutíua (Maranhão); the stress statement is given for the language as a whole. Eiró 2002 describes Tembé of the Gurupi river (c. 400 speakers, two age-graded varieties). Bendor-Samuel 1972 (unopened) is Guajajara of the Santa Inês area (Maranhão), where his 1961 fieldwork began.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the extracted text we hold of da Silva 2010 at the stated lines/pages. (2) The deciding source is a 2010 historical-comparative PhD whose synchronic phonology section is brief and second-order (built on Eiró 2001), but it is a modern specialist work covering both dialects, and two independent sources downloaded now agree with the classification: Harrison & Harrison 2013 (SIL, decades of Guajajára fieldwork) state final stress on nouns/verbs, and Eiró 2002's Tembé transcriptions show final stress plus penult stress before negative -i exactly as coded. Carvalho 2001 and Castro 2017 (both downloaded, open) are silent on stress. (3) The two works that could deepen the record — Bendor-Samuel 1972 (SIL PL 37) and Eiró 2001 (UFPA MA) — are not yet obtained and not fetchable by automated download (MPG copy restricted; sil.org could not be reached by automated download; Eiró 2001 not digitized at UFPA). sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: No explicit stress rule (segmental phonology summary of Eiró 2001). Transcriptions mark stress word-finally ([pa'ko] 'banana', [ki'haw] 'rede', [da'war] 'onça', [pi'tun] 'noite') and on the penult before negative -i ([na'ʔari] 'não caio', [naɛ'saki] 'não vejo', [na'hemi] 'não venho').
sources.note: Silent on the rule; the paper covers only segmental phonemes, allophony and two age-graded varieties (I: speakers over 35, II: under 35) of Tembé of the Gurupi river (Pará/Maranhão border). Its transcriptions are compatible with the Harrison & Harrison final-stress statement.
